where: Windward Stair I & II (the switchback mountain route) + the Wind-Eye and Thunderroost spurs
mood: The Long Climb — airy, building, breath-quickening; each phrase re-launches a step higher so the loop feels like ascent.
core_styles: 16-bit console RPG soundtrack from the mid-1990s
retro sampled-chip instruments with the warm echo of a 16-bit sound chip
high pulse-wave lead climbing in stepwise terraces
steady ascending arpeggio like footsteps on stone
sampled 16-bit marching snare and kick on a steady march beat
white-noise wind swell cresting every four bars
mountain climbing route theme, determined and airy, sunset thinning to cold blue

sections.name: Intro
sections.text: {two bars of sampled marching snare and kick alone set the pace, then the lead strikes the climbing figure and the theme begins}

sections.name: Main Theme
sections.text: {the climbing melody: a rising leap that overshoots, then a stepwise settle, the phrase then re-launched a step higher; hummable and determined, footstep arpeggio under it}

sections.name: Main Theme Higher
sections.text: {the theme sequenced one step higher, brighter and fuller, a bell counter-line glinting, the wind swell cresting at each switchback}

sections.name: Bridge
sections.text: {contrast: a breath on a ledge, F sharp minor and D major, longer notes looking out over the drop, the drums thinning to hat and kick, then a snare roll building back up}

sections.name: Main Theme Return
sections.text: {the climb resumes at full stride, the theme at its brightest; the last bar steps down to the E dominant and voice-leads straight back up into the theme}

_note: 2026-10 retro + tempo pass: motif dropped (it pinned the take to ~90 BPM); era-first anchor, retro kit/bass; opening shape chosen per scene.
